notes:
I couldn't write these notes. The research tool hit its usage limit on my first try, before any page loaded, so I haven't read anything from the sites you listed.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. Writing the notes now would mean using my own memory and unchecked URLs, so I've left them out entirely.

Ask again in a new turn when the tool is available. I'll start with these sources:

- **The traditional reading:** Enduring Word (Psalm 28), Bible Hub's Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages, Precept Austin's Psalm 28 page, and Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*.
- **Protestant traditions:** Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Ligonier or The Gospel Coalition (Reformed), Desiring God or GTY (Baptist), and LCMS or 1517 (Lutheran). These will matter most for whether it's right to pray "repay them" in v. 4–5, and for who "His anointed" is in v. 8 (David, the king, or Christ).
- **Other views:** the NET Bible notes for wording questions like "Pit" (v. 1), "holy sanctuary" (v. 2) and "carry them" (v. 9). For the Catholic reading, Augustine's sermon on this psalm at New Advent. Catholic Bibles number the psalms differently, so I'll check whether it's filed as Psalm 27 there.
